summary: A 1931-32 NPS rustic stone lookout on Crater Lake's rim, part of a historic fire network, restored in 1999 and still reached by a short popular hike.

facts.design: Two-story stone-and-frame structure, National Park Service rustic style

staffing.status: staffed every fire season through 1974, intermittently since; firelookout.com describes current summer staffing

access.note: Within Crater Lake National Park; reached by a short, popular hike from the Watchman Overlook on Rim Drive. No vehicle access to the summit.

visit.trail_note: Short hike from Watchman Overlook, Rim Drive, to the summit of Watchman Peak.

events.note: Construction by NPS crews began; completed early in the 1932 fire season. NHLR gives 1931 as the build year; the structure's own NRHP/Wikipedia record gives 1932 as the completion/build year.
NPS staffed it every fire season through 1974, intermittently afterward.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, December 1, 1988 (ref #88002626).
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, December 1, 2002.

evidence.supports: Built 1931, completed 1932, most-visited lookout, restored 1999, in service
evidence.quote: The imposing two-story stone structure was built by crews under the supervision of the U.S. National Park Service in 1931 and was completed in the early part of the fire season in 1932. ... Carefully restored in 1999, the lookout is in service.

evidence.supports: Most visited lookout claim and hike access
evidence.quote: Reached by a short hike from the west rim overlook, it is possibly the most visited lookout in Oregon (Lava Butte may claim that title).

evidence.supports: Elevation, peak naming, architect, construction year, dual fire/museum purpose, NRHP listing date
evidence.quote: The lookout structure (designated "Building 168") was constructed in 1932, and served the dual purpose of fire lookout and trail museum. The lookout location was selected by Merel S. Sager of the National Park Service Landscape Division.

evidence.supports: Fire detection network, ranger staffing with radio, CCC involvement, staffed through 1974
evidence.quote: A trained observer, usually a park ranger, staffed the lookout and kept in contact with the fire dispatcher at the park headquarters on short-wave radio. During the 1930s, the Civilian Conservation Corps also provided observers. The National Park Service staffed the Watchman Lookout Station during fire season until 1974 and intermittently since then.

evidence.supports: Peak named 1886 by William Gladstone Steel
evidence.quote: Watchman Peak was named by William Gladstone Steel in 1886 when he brought a survey team to Crater Lake to measure its depth.

evidence.supports: Built 1931, two-story stone and frame cab, restored, staffed in summer
evidence.quote: Built in 1931, this 2-story stone and frame cab has recently been restored and is staffed in the summer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com give 1931 as the build year; Wikipedia's infobox and NRHP record give 1932, describing 1932 as when construction/completion occurred. The story presents both: built 1931, completed early in the 1932 fire season, following NHLR's account of the timeline.

notes_for_editor: Minor date ambiguity: NHLR says built 1931/completed 1932; NRHP record/Wikipedia infobox say built 1932. No rental program; it's a day-use hike within Crater Lake National Park.
